title: AI trip-readiness assistant
offer: Proposed trip-readiness pack for a 7–14 day multi-city trip: identify itinerary timing conflicts, check travel between stops, flag budget mismatches and suggest a fallback day. Show source links and checks; traveller verifies and approves bookings. No human concierge, autonomous booking or guaranteed disruption protection.

segments.name: First-time multi-city travellers
segments.description: Two or three unfamiliar cities; transport and timing decisions compound.

segments.name: Families with complex itineraries
segments.description: Multiple stops with meal, rest and accessibility constraints.

segments.name: Group-trip organisers
segments.description: Four or more people with different budgets and preferences.

segments.name: Simple city-break travellers
segments.description: One city, a few saved places and flexible days.

segments.name: Frequent work travellers
segments.description: Flights and hotels already managed; limited leisure planning.

market_sources.title: Mindtrip: free AI travel companion
market_sources.text: Mindtrip advertises a free travel app with personalised itineraries, group collaboration, maps, recommendations and booking receipt organisation. Implication: a paid generic itinerary assistant competes against an established free bundle. This is a vendor feature claim, not proof of customer demand.

market_sources.title: Wanderlog: free collaborative planning
market_sources.text: Wanderlog says its core planning experience remains free, without limiting trips or the number of collaborators. A paid Pro tier adds premium features. Implication: group collaboration alone is not sufficient differentiation. This source does not establish current Pro pricing.

market_sources.title: TripIt Pro: US$49 per year
market_sources.text: TripIt advertises Pro at US$49 per year, with flight alerts, alternative flight options and other practical travel assistance. This is an annual USD competitor benchmark, not a GBP per-trip equivalent or measured willingness to pay for our proposed product.

method.data: 1,000 deterministic fictional scenarios, 200 per buying situation; equal allocation is not a market estimate.
method.decision_rule: Trip-readiness: scenario eligibility × logistic price response. Basic itinerary: 35% of readiness eligibility and 60% of its price thresholds. Individual thresholds discretise the curve for inspectability.
method.uncertainty: Low/high use 0.6× / 1.4× scenario choices, capped at segment count; sensitivity bounds, NOT confidence intervals.
method.provenance: Competitor features/pricing are sourced. Eligibility, GBP price midpoints, slope, concept effects and bounds are unvalidated author assumptions. No model calls; no revenue forecasts.
